question: A line cuts two concentric circles. The length of chords formed by this line on the circles is 6 cm and 18 cm. Find the difference in the squares of the radii of two circles.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in squares of radii = (Half of larger chord)² − (Half of smaller chord)²

⇒ R² − r² = (18 ÷ 2)² − (6 ÷ 2)²

⇒ R² − r² = 9² − 3²

⇒ R² − r² = 81 − 9 = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of inner chord (CD) = 6 cm

Length of outer chord (AB) = 18 cm

**Formula Used:**

A perpendicular drawn from the center of a circle to a chord bisects the chord.

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let O be the center of the concentric circles and OM (d) be the perpendicular drawn to the chords.

⇒ Half of inner chord (MD) = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 cm

⇒ Half of outer chord (MB) = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 cm

⇒ Let the inner radius be r and outer radius be R.

⇒ In right-angled ΔOMD:

⇒ r² = d² + 3²

⇒ d² = r² − 9 ... (Equation 1)

⇒ In right-angled ΔOMB:

⇒ R² = d² + 9²

⇒ d² = R² − 81 ... (Equation 2)

⇒ Equating Equation 1 and Equation 2:

⇒ r² − 9 = R² − 81

⇒ R² − r² = 81 − 9

⇒ R² − r² = 72

**∴ The correct answer is 72 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular to a Chord

A line drawn from the center of a circle perpendicular to a chord always bisects the chord into two equal segments.

Area of Annulus (Ring)

The region bounded between two concentric circles is called an annulus. Its area is calculated by subtracting the inner circle area from the outer circle area: Area = π(R² − r²).

Concentric Circles

Circles that share the same center point but have different radii are known as concentric circles. Any line intersecting both circles forms segments that are symmetrical around the perpendicular from the center.
